Series::digamma¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::digamma() const
Series& Series::digamma_()
Series& Series::digamma_() const

What It Does¶

Computes the digamma function elementwise. Digamma, written psi, is the logarithmic derivative of the gamma function:

psi(x) = d/dx ln( Gamma(x) ) = Gamma'(x) / Gamma(x)

It is the function that lgamma() differentiates to, so it turns up in exactly the places lgamma does — the gradient of a beta function, the score of a gamma or Dirichlet density, the derivative of a binomial coefficient with respect to its arguments.

Anchor facts to carry:

  • psi(1) = -0.5772157, the negative of the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

  • psi(2) = 0.4227843.

  • The recurrence psi(x + 1) = psi(x) + 1/x links consecutive arguments by a single reciprocal. It is the digamma image of Gamma(x + 1) = x * Gamma(x).

  • psi(x) grows like ln(x) for large x; it is negative on (0, 1.4616...) and positive after.

  • At signed zero, the one-sided pole is preserved: digamma(+0.0) is -inf and digamma(-0.0) is +inf. Negative integer poles return NaN.

  • On the intervals between the negative-integer poles psi(x) is finite. The value is recovered from the positive axis through the reflection identity psi(1 - x) - psi(x) = pi / tan(pi x).

digamma() is an out-of-place unary transform: shape and platform are preserved. Floating-point input keeps its dtype; integral input is promoted to float64. digamma_() overwrites floating-point storage in place.

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series or Series& A Series with the same shape as self, each element replaced by psi(x). digamma_() returns a reference to the mutated current series.

An integral input is promoted to float64; a floating-point input keeps its dtype. The in-place form requires floating-point storage because an integral receiver cannot represent the result.

Gradient¶

digamma() is differentiable. Its derivative is the trigamma function, which is polygamma(1, x):

d/dx psi(x) = psi'(x) = polygamma(1, x)

The backward pass evaluates trigamma directly with a recurrence-plus-asymptotic routine, so the sensitivity is accurate across the whole positive axis and for negative non-integers. Trigamma is strictly positive wherever it is defined, so a tracked digamma() always contributes a positive local slope.

At zero and negative-integer poles, trigamma diverges to +inf. A reverse pass through such an input therefore produces an infinite local sensitivity even when the corresponding digamma value is NaN at a negative integer.

In-Place Form¶

digamma_() is the in-place sibling of digamma(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — digamma_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 5.0});

auto& ref = x.digamma_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.57721566, 0.42278434, 1.5061177]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. On the positive integers, consecutive values differ by a reciprocal.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0}).digamma());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.5772, 0.4228, 0.9228, 1.2561]

psi(2) = psi(1) + 1/1, psi(3) = psi(2) + 1/2, psi(4) = psi(3) + 1/3.

Example 2. Half-integer arguments.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.5, 1.5, 2.5}).digamma());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-1.9635, 0.0365, 0.7032]

psi(0.5) = -gamma - 2 ln 2, about -1.9635.

Example 3. The recurrence, checked directly. psi(x + 1) - psi(x) equals 1/x.

auto x = pluss::make_series({2.0, 3.0, 7.0});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.add(1.0).digamma().sub(x.digamma()));
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.reciprocal());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.5000, 0.3333, 0.1429]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.5000, 0.3333, 0.1429]

Example 4. Signed zero records which side approaches the pole. Negative integer poles are NaN, while negative non-integers remain finite through reflection.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({0.0, -0.0, -1.0, -0.5}).digamma());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[-inf, inf, nan, 0.0365]

Example 5. The backward pass is trigamma. With the input tracked, a reverse pass fills the sensitivity with polygamma(1, x) evaluated at each element.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.5, 2.5, 3.5});
x.tracks_slope_(true);
x.digamma().sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity());
pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({1.5, 2.5, 3.5}).polygamma(1));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.9348, 0.4904, 0.3304]
Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0.9348, 0.4904, 0.3304]

The sensitivity matches polygamma(1, x) term for term.

Example 6. Integral inputs are promoted to float64 rather than rejected.

pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({1, 2, 3}).digamma());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.5772, 0.4228, 0.9228]

Example 7. digamma_() overwrites the current storage in place.

auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0, 3.0});
a.digamma_();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, a);

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[-0.5772, 0.4228, 0.9228]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Signed zero returns a signed infinity: +0.0 maps to -inf, while -0.0 maps to +inf. Negative integer poles return NaN.

  • The gradient is trigamma and diverges to +inf at those poles.

  • For the derivatives of ln Gamma beyond the first, use polygamma(n, x); digamma(x) is the n = 0 case.

  • An integral series is promoted to float64; the result is never integral.

Summary¶

digamma() is psi(x) = d/dx ln Gamma(x) as a shape-preserving unary transform:

  • psi(1) = -gamma, psi(2) = 1 - gamma, and psi(x + 1) = psi(x) + 1/x

  • signed infinities at zero, NaN at negative integers, and finite values at negative non-integers

  • differentiable, with backward polygamma(1, x); the gradient diverges at the poles

  • integral inputs promote to float64

  • digamma_() is the in-place form

See Also¶

  • Series::lgamma: the function digamma is the derivative of.

  • Series::polygamma: the higher derivatives of ln Gamma; digamma is polygamma(0, .) and its gradient is polygamma(1, .).

  • Series::mvlgamma: the multivariate log-gamma, whose gradient is a sum of digamma terms.

  • Series::beta: its log gradient is a difference of digamma values.
